subject: Re: Quantify Health - tranche scope & repricing / implementation sequence
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@quantifyhealth.com>

Cc: carlos.mendez@quantifyhealth.com; legal@quantifyhealth.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Request: tranche addition + repricing for Order Form QH-0421

Diego —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We had a cross-functional follow-up this morning and would like to propose a tranche-based amendment to our current Order Form (QH-0421). High level: add a committed GPU tranche for pilot (12 weeks), then an additional production tranche thereafter. We expect top-line consumption to grow ~2.5x after pilot.

Key asks:
- Add a 12-week pilot tranche (4x V100-equivalent) starting Jun 15.
- Add option to convert pilot to production with a single-sided notice and an 8-week lead time.
- Reprice the production tier to reflect volume: target ~18% blended discount vs current rate.
- Clarify implementation sequence and acceptance criteria in SOW.

Can you outline the change order approach (MSA vs Order Form amendment), an aggressive timeline for approvals, and what legal artifacts you need from our side? I can loop in procurement/admin if useful.

Thanks —
Ellen
Ellen Park
Head of Platform Ops, Quantify Health

Ellen —

Appreciate the clear ask and timeline. High-level approach: we can do a scoped Change Order that amends the existing Order Form and references the MSA (no need for a full MSA amendment). That keeps signature surface area small and allows the pilot to be timeboxed.

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) Redwood (Legal + Pricing) to produce a redline of the Order Form + a short SOW exhibit that spells out pilot acceptance criteria and conversion mechanics (we’ll include an explicit notice window).
2) Quantify to confirm desired pilot start date (you mentioned Jun 15) and provide any security/compliance constraints that would affect onboarding timeline.
3) Both legal teams exchange redlines; we aim to align commercial terms (pricing/tranche discounts) before DocuSign.

I’ve looped in Laura (legal) and Marcus (pricing). Marcus — can you draft a blended rate proposal for the production tier with the 18% target and a fallback band if volumes undershoot? Laura — will you take point on the Order Form redline + short SOW?

I’ll coordinate timelines with Ellen; we should try to get commercial agreement this week to leave time for legal back-and-forth.

Best,

Attached are Redwood’s initial redlines to the Order Form and a short SOW exhibit that defines: pilot scope (capacity, start/end), acceptance tests (throughput and latency gates), conversion notice mechanism, and implementation responsibilities. Notable commercial/legal points we call out:
- We treat the pilot tranche as a time-limited committed capacity with pro-rated billing if the pilot terminates early.
- Conversion to production requires an executed Change Order, and we propose an 8-week lead time for capacity provisioning.
- We added explicit language on resource substitution and fallback model variants to preserve availability.
- We included a limited SLA exception during pilot (reduced credits) and a hard date for acceptance testing.

Please review the redlines and the SOW markup. If Quantify has internal procurement/legal language that needs to flow into the Order Form, please send your counter redlines. For timing: Marcus will circulate a pricing note by EOD Monday (24 May).

Laura / Diego —

Thanks for the redlines. Attached are Quantify’s counter-markups. Main items:
- We want the pilot conversion to be an operational toggle (conversion notice + auto-escalation) rather than requiring a separate signed Change Order — this reduces procurement cycles for us.
- Requesting tighter SLAs during production tranche (higher uptime credit thresholds) and limiting Redwood’s right to substitute GPUs without prior notification except for emergency failovers.
- Need to confirm data handling and retention clauses in the SOW (we flagged a documentation request).

We’re open to a compromise where the pilot conversion triggers an internal purchase order commitment and a short executed amendment to finalize price, which should be quicker than a full Change Order. Please review our counter and provide a commercial response to the pricing band.

Carlos Mendez
Senior Procurement Manager, Quantify Health

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 15:18:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing proposal: blended production band + pilot pricing mechanics

Team —

Following Diego’s ask, attached is a proposed commercial compromise. Headline: a two-band approach that balances Quantify’s desire for fast conversion with Redwood’s need to reserve capacity and protect unit economics.

Proposal summary: 
- Pilot tranche (12 weeks): flat pilot rate at 70% of current on-demand list (billed weekly, pro-rated if cancelled during pilot).
- Conversion mechanics: upon customer notice to convert, Redwood will hold production capacity for 8 weeks at an agreed "conversion hold" rate (50% of the full production weekly charge) while provisioning. If Quantify confirms conversion within that 8-week window, the blended production price (agreed below) applies retroactively to week 1 of production.
- Blended production price: target 18% discount vs current list, with a floor of 12% if average monthly consumption in the first 90 days is below 70% of forecast.
- If Quantify requires the faster auto-toggle (no signed amendment), we ask for a 4% premium on the blended price to account for provisioning risk.

Implementation sequence we propose:
1) Sign short Change Order that adds the pilot tranche and SOW exhibit (2–3 business days).
2) Pilot onboarding (target Jun 15 start).
3) Conversion notice window and provisioning (8 weeks).
4) Production go-live and retrospective billing reconciliation per the blended-pricing clause.

If that tracks, Laura and Quantify Legal can update the language on the conversion mechanism and SLA thresholds. Happy to hop on a 30-min call to finalize.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference
